judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives in the same PRIMARY THREE 'Capacity' topic (Sub-Theme Secondary Measures, Theme Mensuration and Geometry). The first objective identifies the litre as a unit of measuring capacity; the second identifies the need for accuracy when measuring liquids. They share substantive conceptual coherence around capacity/liquid measurement (shared LC tags 'capacity','measurement'). However both are same-rank (PRIMARY THREE, rank 2) 'identify' objectives with no clear developmental dependency—accuracy concerns an attitude toward measurement rather than requiring prior unit knowledge as a strict foundation—so no directional buildsTowards is substantiated. Objective numbering (1 vs 3) and shared hierarchy/page proximity are not themselves semantic evidence. relatesTo best captures complementary measurement skills.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY TWO Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Three dimensional shapes' (Sub-Theme Shapes, Theme Mensuration and Geometry). The first asks pupils to mention real-world home objects that are cylinders and spheres; the second asks pupils to identify and count the corners of a cube and a cuboid. These are complementary 3D-shapes skills within one topic but address different solids and different cognitive actions (naming/recognizing familiar objects vs. analyzing/counting geometric features). No source evidence establishes that proficiency in one supports success in the other, and they share the same rank with no ordering signal, so a directional buildsTowards is unsupported. Substantive conceptual coherence within the 3D-shapes topic warrants relatesTo. Token/trigram overlap is dominated by boilerplate ('pupils','should','able') and the LC overlap is only 'the', which is not semantic evidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Topic '2. Subtraction' (same rank 0). First objective is 'subtract from whole numbers not greater than 9'; second is 'crosscheck accuracy in subtraction'. Crosschecking the accuracy of a subtraction presupposes the ability to perform subtraction, so proficiency in the first substantively supports success in the second, justifying a same-rank developmental direction from first to second. This is a genuine skill dependency, not merely shared hierarchy or the 'subtraction' token overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Addition' (Sub-Theme/Theme Basic Operations). The first is an affective/awareness objective ('mention the need for correct addition of numbers and fractions in everyday activities'); the second is a procedural computation skill ('add 3 numbers taking two at a time'). They share substantive conceptual coherence around addition and reinforce each other, but neither is a clear developmental prerequisite for the other: appreciating the need for correct addition does not depend on this specific grouping technique, and the technique does not require the awareness objective. Same rank (PRIMARY THREE, gap 0) provides no directional basis, so a symmetric relatesTo is warranted over buildsTowards.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under the same Theme (Mensuration and Geometry) and Sub-Theme (Shapes): the first asks pupils to mention solid (3D) shapes in homes and environment, the second to mention square, rectangular and circular (2D) shapes in homes. They are parallel, complementary shape-recognition skills applied to the everyday environment, but sit under distinct sibling Topics (Three dimensional vs Two dimensional shapes) at the same grade rank (0). No substantive evidence shows proficiency in one enables success in the other, so a developmental direction is unwarranted; the strong shared context and skill coherence support a symmetric relatesTo. Text/trigram overlap and shared LC 'shapes' token reflect parallel phrasing, not dependency.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Addition'. The second SFI (objective 1: add two whole numbers from 1 to 3 with sum less than 5) is a foundational single-digit addition skill, while the first SFI (objective 4: add 2-digit whole numbers with sum not greater than 40 without exchanging or renaming) is a substantively more complex extension involving larger, multi-digit addends. Proficiency in the simpler small-number addition supports success in the more complex 2-digit addition, so buildsTowards runs second_to_first (simpler source to advanced target). Though same grade rank, the ordered objective sequence (1 vs 4) and clear increase in numeric range/complexity provide substantive developmental evidence.
